lesson_title: Eight Blocks Across, Six Blocks Up: Distance, Midpoint and Gradient
hook_text: Walking the streets is 14 blocks. Cutting across the field is 10. That gap is the whole formula.
clip_script: A town laid out in blocks. You're at your friend's gate; her cousin lives eight blocks east and six blocks north. Walk the streets and that's fourteen blocks. But there's an open field between you. Cut straight across — how far? Eight across, six up, right-angled triangle. Sixty-four plus thirty-six is one hundred. Square root, ten. The shortcut is ten blocks. That's the whole distance formula, and coordinates just tell you the eight and the six without pacing them out. Now the middle. Two friends at house number three and house number eleven meet at house number seven — you add and you halve. On a grid you do that twice, once across, once up. And here's the one thing to brand in: middle means ADD and halve. Distance and steepness both SUBTRACT. Speaking of steepness — gradient is how much it goes up, divided by how much it goes across. Rise over run. Three over four means for every four steps forward, it climbs three. Flat field, gradient zero. Straight wall? Undefined, not zero — there's no across to divide by. And two lines are at right angles when you flip one gradient upside down and change its sign. Multiply them and you get negative one, every single time. That's your protractor, on paper.
visual_style: Overhead grid-town animation: a walking route in one colour, a diagonal shortcut in another; house numbers averaging into a meeting point; a ramp and a hill road tilting to show gradient; two lines snapping to a right angle.
pacing: Quick through the walk, a beat on 'ten', deliberate on the add-versus-subtract rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and classify any quadrilateral on the grid without guessing.
